root_cause.text: The quota data objects (struct gfs2_quota_data) were freed without being removed from the global LRU list (gfs2_qd_lru), allowing the shrinker to access freed memory (use-after-free).
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "Commit a475c5dd16e5 started freeing quota data objects during filesystem shutdown ... but it failed to remove these objects from the LRU list, causing LRU list corruption. This caused use-after-free when the shrinker (gfs2_qd_shrink_scan) tried to access already-freed objects on the LRU list." The patch adds `list_lru_del_obj(&gfs2_qd_lru, &qd->qd_lru)` before `gfs2_qd_dispose(qd)` in `qd_put()` to correct this.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a475c5dd16e57c570113eccba51955b5df8bb052
Author: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 23 17:15:47 2023 +0200

    gfs2: Free quota data objects synchronously
    
    In gfs2_quota_cleanup(), wait for the quota data objects to be freed
    before returning.  Otherwise, there is no guarantee that the quota data
    objects will be gone when their kmem cache is destroyed.
    
    Signed-off-by: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>

diff --git a/fs/gfs2/quota.c b/f
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit ensures quota data objects are removed from the global LRU list before being freed. In gfs2_quota_cleanup, objects with zero refcount are marked dead and removed from LRU via list_lru_del (line 'list_lru_del(&gfs2_qd_lru, &qd->qd_lru);') before disposal. In qd_put, when the journal is not live, lockref_mark_dead is called followed by gfs2_qd_dispose, which performs list_del_init(&qd->qd_lru). gfs2_qd_dispose itself always removes from LRU before scheduling RCU freeing. The atomic_dec of sd_quota_count is moved to gfs2_qd_dealloc, ensuring proper synchronization. Thus the vulnerable construct (freeing without LRU removal) is absent and the fix is fully present.
